issues.title: cloneDeep strips Temporal.* instances to {} (loses prototype, internal slots, instanceof)
issues.body:
`cloneDeep` does not preserve `Temporal.*` instances. The clone loses its prototype chain, internal slots, and `instanceof` identity — the result is a plain `{}` with no Temporal methods. `isEqual(original, clone)` then returns `false`, which breaks downstream patterns that depend on "clone then compare" (dirty-state checks, undo/redo snapshots, form models, etc.).

### Reproduction

```js
import { cloneDeep, isEqual } from 'lodash';
import 'temporal-polyfill/global';

const date = Temporal.PlainDate.from('2026-05-20');
const clone = cloneDeep(date);

console.log(clone);                              // {}
console.log(clone instanceof Temporal.PlainDate); // false
console.log(isEqual(date, clone));                // false
```

Affects every Temporal value type: `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime`, `PlainYearMonth`, `PlainMonthDay`, `Instant`, `ZonedDateTime`, `Duration`.

### Environment

- lodash 4.18.1
- temporal-polyfill 0.3.2 (same shape will hit native `Temporal` once browsers ship it — the data lives in internal slots, not enumerable own properties)
- Node 24 (also reproduces in jsdom / happy-dom / browser)

### Why this matters

Temporal types are immutable, so the correct treatment is to return the same reference (no copy needed). lodash currently treats them as plain objects and walks own properties — which on a Temporal instance is the empty set, so the prototype, internal slots, and `instanceof` identity are all lost.

### Workaround

`cloneDeepWith` with a customizer that short-circuits Temporal instances:

```js
import { cloneDeepWith } from 'lodash';

const isTemporal = (v) =>
  v != null && typeof v === 'object' && (
    v instanceof Temporal.PlainDate ||
    v instanceof Temporal.PlainTime ||
    v instanceof Temporal.PlainDateTime ||
    v instanceof Temporal.PlainYearMonth ||
    v instanceof Temporal.PlainMonthDay ||
    v instanceof Temporal.Instant ||
    v instanceof Temporal.ZonedDateTime ||
    v instanceof Temporal.Duration
  );

export const cloneDeep = (value) =>
  cloneDeepWith(value, (v) => (isTemporal(v) ? v : undefined));
```

This works but means every consumer of Temporal-bearing state has to swap their import. A built-in fix would let `cloneDeep` Just Work for the upcoming Stage 3 Temporal proposal.

### Suggested fix

Detect Temporal instances in the clone walker and return them by reference (they're immutable). A symmetric fix in `isEqual` would also help — `isEqual(PlainDate.from('2026-05-20'), PlainDate.from('2026-05-20'))` currently returns `false` because the Temporal `Object.prototype.toString` tag isn't in `equalByTag`'s known list.

comments.body:
This is an inherent issue with any new builtin type, for cloneDeep.

The proper way to clone a Temporal object is eg `Temporal.PlainDate.from(plainDate)`, for future reference.

issues.title: Update CVEs for Lodash.* per-method packages
issues.body: Atomic packages like [lodash.set](https://npmjs.com/lodash.set) still have vulnerabilities that have been patched in main lodash. These get millions of downloads weekly and their vulnerabilities should be patched to make other packages not have them. Simply rebuild these packages and update them as a new version number
issues.author: tj-commits

comments.body:
## Security Analysis: CVE-2020-28500 Unfixed in Individual Packages

I conducted a vulnerability intelligence scan and found that **lodash.trim** and **lodash.trimend** remain vulnerable to CVE-2020-28500 (ReDoS) with **no fix available**.

### Affected Packages

| Package | Latest Version | Weekly Downloads | Fix Status |
|---------|---------------|------------------|------------|
| `lodash.trim` | 4.5.1 | ~118,000 | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.trimend` | 4.5.1 | ~111,000 | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash` (main) | 4.17.21 | ~52M | Fixed |

### Technical Details

The OSV database (GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9) explicitly lists these packages with `last_affected: 4.5.1` rather than a `fixed` version, confirming no patch exists.

**Vulnerability**: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)  
**CVSS v3.1**: 5.3 (Medium) - `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L`  
**Affected Functions**: `trim()`, `trimEnd()` in the vulnerable packages

The main `lodash` package was fixed in commit `c4847ebe7d14540bb28a8b932a9ce1b9ecbfee1a` (PR #5065), but this fix was never propagated to the individual method packages.

### Impact Assessment

- Combined ~229,000 weekly downloads still using vulnerable code
- Users chose individual packages specifically for bundle size optimization
- These users may not realize they're using different packages than the patched main lodash

### Recommended Actions

**Option 1: Patch and Release** (Preferred)
- Apply the fix from PR #5065 to `lodash.trim` and `lodash.trimend`
- Release as version 4.5.2 or 4.6.0

**Option 2: Deprecate**
- Mark these packages as deprecated on npm
- Add deprecation message pointing to main `lodash` package or native `String.prototype.trim()`

**Option 3: Combination**
- Release patched version AND add deprecation notice recommending migration

### Migration Guidance for Users

```javascript
// VULNERABLE - do not use
const trim = require('lodash.trim');

// FIXED - use main lodash package
const { trim } = require('lodash');
// or
const trim = require('lodash/trim');

// ALTERNATIVE - use native JavaScript
const trimmed = str.trim();
const trimmedEnd = str.trimEnd();
```

### References

- [GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9)
- [CVE-2020-28500](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-28500)
- [Fix PR #5065](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/5065)
- [OSV Entry](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-29mw-wpgm-hmr9)

I'm happy to assist with creating a PR to apply the fix or add deprecation notices. This ties directly into the STA-funded security work mentioned in #6034.

---
*Identified via ATLAS Vulnerability Intelligence scan - 2026-02-26*

comments.body:
## Expanded Scope: 9 Unfixed Individual Packages Identified

Following up on my previous analysis, I've completed a comprehensive scan and identified **7 additional individual lodash packages** with unfixed vulnerabilities beyond `lodash.trim` and `lodash.trimend`.

### Complete List of Affected Packages (~40M combined weekly downloads)

#### ReDoS (CVE-2020-28500) - Medium Severity
| Package | Last Version | Weekly Downloads | Status |
|---------|-------------|------------------|--------|
| `lodash.trim` | 4.5.1 | ~3M | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.trimend` | 4.5.1 | ~1M | **UNFIXED** |

#### Command Injection (CVE-2021-23337) - HIGH Severity (CVSS 7.2)
| Package | Last Version | Weekly Downloads | Status |
|---------|-------------|------------------|--------|
| `lodash.template` | 4.5.0 | ~8M | **UNFIXED** |

This is particularly concerning as it allows arbitrary code execution when untrusted input is passed to template options.

#### Prototype Pollution (CVE-2020-8203) - HIGH Severity (CVSS 7.4)
| Package | Last Version | Weekly Downloads | Status |
|---------|-------------|------------------|--------|
| `lodash.set` | 4.3.2 | ~15M | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.setwith` | 4.3.2 | ~3M | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.update` | 4.10.2 | ~1M | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.updatewith` | 4.10.2 | ~500K | **UNFIXED** |
| `lodash.pick` | 4.4.0 | ~12M | **UNFIXED** |

### PR #6118 Updated

I've expanded PR #6118 to cover all 9 affected packages:
- README.md now includes a comprehensive security warning table
- Migration guide covers all vulnerability types with specific examples
- Added npm commands and workarounds for transitive dependencies

### Recommendations for TSC

Given the scale (40M+ weekly downloads of vulnerable code), the TSC may want to consider:

1. **Short-term**: Merge PR #6118 to document the issue and guide affected users
2. **Medium-term**: Publish patched versions of individual packages (even if just to bump to latest main package code)
3. **Long-term**: Add npm deprecation warnings to guide users to the main package

### Security References

- CVE-2020-28500 (ReDoS): https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-28500
- CVE-2021-23337 (Command Injection): https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-23337  
- CVE-2020-8203 (Prototype Pollution): https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-8203

I'm happy to assist with any additional documentation or contribute to patching efforts if the TSC decides to update the individual packages.

comments.author: tj-commits

comments.body:
@tj-commits That's a solid suggestion. Making the atomic packages depend on and re-export from the main lodash package would have several advantages:

**Benefits of the dependency approach:**
1. **Automatic security fix propagation** - Any future patches to the main package would immediately benefit all atomic package users
2. **No code changes for downstream users** - Projects using `lodash.trim` or `lodash.set` would continue to work without modification
3. **Single point of maintenance** - Security fixes only need to be applied once, reducing maintenance burden

The implementation would be straightforward - each atomic package would simply re-export the corresponding function from the main package:

```javascript
// lodash.trim/index.js
module.exports = require('lodash/trim');
```

This approach and PR #6118 (documentation/migration guidance) aren't mutually exclusive - they complement each other. The dependency approach fixes the vulnerability transparently, while documentation helps users understand the security context and make informed decisions about their dependency strategy.

I'm supportive of whichever approach the maintainers prefer. If the team decides to go the dependency route and would like help with implementation PRs for the atomic packages, I'm happy to contribute.
comments.author: abhu85

comments.body:
Hi @jdalton and lodash maintainers,

Following up on the CVE-2020-28500 (ReDoS) disclosure posted on 2026-02-26.

**Current situation:**
- The standalone packages `lodash.trim` and `lodash.trimend` remain vulnerable
- These packages have ~3.5M weekly downloads combined
- The fix exists in main `lodash` (4.17.21+) but was never backported to the atomic packages

**Community suggestion:**
@tj-commits proposed having atomic packages depend on the main lodash package, which would automatically propagate security fixes. This seems like a sustainable long-term solution.

**Proposed paths forward:**
1. **Deprecate vulnerable packages** with npm deprecation notice pointing to main lodash
2. **Publish patched versions** of `lodash.trim`/`lodash.trimend`
3. **Accept PR #6118** to document the security status and migration path

Any of these would help the community make informed decisions. Happy to assist with implementation.

If there's no response by **2026-03-28** (30 days), I'll proceed with responsible disclosure through the OpenJS Foundation CNA process.

Thank you for your time.

@tj-commits Thanks for the detailed feedback - you're right about the download counts being inaccurate. I've pushed a fix to PR #6118:

**Corrected download counts (from npm API):**
| Package | Previous | Actual |
|---------|----------|--------|
| Combined | ~40M | **~4.8M** |
| lodash.template | ~8M | **~2.4M** |
| lodash.set | ~15M | **~1.2M** |
| lodash.pick | ~12M | **~1.1M** |
| lodash.trim | ~3M | **~60K** |
| lodash.trimend | ~1M | **~50K** |

**Fixed the npm overrides section** to point to your `@lodash-modularized` packages instead of the broken direct lodash override.

One clarification: PR #5065 *is* the fix for CVE-2020-28500. The commit `c4847ebe7d` message explicitly states: "*This prevents potential ReDoS attacks using `_.toNumber` and `_.trim*` as potential attack vectors. Closes #5065.*" So that reference was accurate.

Thanks for creating lodash-modularized - it's a solid community workaround until the official packages get updated.

comments.body:
I have updated the CVEs and advisories issued under the OpenJS Foundation CNA (the 2025-2026 lodash records: CVE-2025-13465, CVE-2026-2950, CVE-2026-4800) with corrected references and per-package affected and patched versions, including the rebuilt per-method packages (`lodash.unset`, `lodash.omit`, `lodash.template`).

The remaining lodash CVEs are older (2018-2021) and are owned by other CNAs (Snyk, HackerOne, DWF), so updating those records or transferring ownership is their call.

One open item before this can be considered fully done: several per-method packages are still published at their old, vulnerable versions, so the gaps reported here are not fully closed yet. Do we want to publish (rebuild from current main) the following packages too?

| Package | Current npm version | Unfixed legacy CVE |
|---|---|---|
| `lodash.set` | 4.3.2 | CVE-2020-8203 |
| `lodash.setwith` | 4.3.2 | CVE-2020-8203 |
| `lodash.update` | 4.10.2 | CVE-2020-8203 |
| `lodash.updatewith` | 4.10.2 | CVE-2020-8203 |
| `lodash.pick` | 4.4.0 | CVE-2020-8203 |
| `lodash.includes` | 4.3.0 | CVE-2020-28500 (toNumber ReDoS) |
| `lodash.merge` | 4.6.2 | CVE-2018-16487 |
| `lodash.mergewith` | 4.6.2 | CVE-2018-16487 |
| `lodash.defaultsdeep` | 4.6.1 | CVE-2019-10744, CVE-2018-3721 |

If these are rebuilt from current main the same way `lodash.unset`, `lodash.omit`, and `lodash.template` were, their fixed version becomes the single source of truth, and we can then ask the owning CNAs to record that fixed version on the corresponding CVEs _and to transfer ownership too_.

Happy to coordinate the CVE side once the packages are published.

issues.title: [Bug]`_.truncate` hangs forever with a zero-length-capable regex `separator`
issues.author: waydeshi

comments.body: To prevent skipping past valid matches while ensuring progress, we should check `if (match[0].length === 0)` and set `separator.lastIndex = match.index + 1`, capped by `substring.length` to avoid out-of-bounds execution.
comments.author: jasminritik26

comments.body: Since `separator.lastIndex` is only updated by `exec` if the regex has the global `g`
comments.author: sayradekayla26

comments.body: RegExp(separator.source, separator.flags + (separator.global ? '' : 'g'))`)

issues.title: _.cloneDeep does not deep clone Map keys (only values)
issues.author: MaansiBisht

comments.body:
Sets only have values, not keys, so I don't think consistency with Set is relevant.

It's certainly different than structuredClone, and you are correct about the third point.

Changing this behavior by default would be a breaking change, so it only makes sense to me to add an option that also clones the keys. (I also think that it would never make sense to clone the keys by default, for the exact reason you highlighted)
comments.author: ljharb

comments.body:
Hi! I'd be happy to work on this if you're open to a PR.

Since `_.cloneDeep` doesn't currently accept an options object, could you share what kind of API you had in mind? My first thought was something like:

```js
_.cloneDeep(value, { cloneMapKeys: true })
```
but that feels like a fairly significant change to the existing API, so I'd appreciate your guidance before I start implementing anything.
